name: PT Multi Garam Utama Tbk

frontmatter.title: Multi Garam Utama: the parts are marked, the price still is not
frontmatter.summary: FOLK's fall is part tape, part disclosure: the IHSG lost -16.7% in October, a holder above five per cent is still selling, and the 4 November release showed Q3 profit was mostly a IDR20.1bn unrealised fair-value gain with cash down to IDR9.9bn [S37][S2][S34]. We rebuild the SOTP on the 30 September balance sheet and correct the bridge: SELL, target Rp26, return -55.1%.
thesis: The market capitalises a data-centre platform; what FOLK actually owns is a water and wastewater treatment supplier with an undisclosed contract value [S6][S5].
The nine-month profit is an accounting result taken below EBIT: Q3 revenue was IDR5.1bn and the operating base has lost money at the EBITDA line in every year since listing [S0][S19].

At 30 September cash was IDR9.9bn against IDR11.5bn of liabilities; the liquidity sits in a IDR105.4bn equity portfolio, IDR57.4bn of it listed, and the parent sold IDR36.6bn of that portfolio in the quarter to fund itself [S34].

Our sum of the parts — the portfolio at fair value, Traya at its annualised run-rate, the media and retail estate at its book residual, less a net holdco deduction and a discount for an unrealised gain — sits far below the share price [S0][S34].
No dated catalyst exists to narrow the discount: no dividend, no buyback, no disclosed asset sale and no upstream cash, while the anchor holder is still selling [S2][S33][S10].

catalysts.event: FY2026 audited accounts — nine-month Traya consolidation and the first test of whether the reported profit converts to cash (statutory deadline, not a company-sourced date)
MSCI consultation feedback closes on Indonesia's proposed standalone status (market-wide)
MSCI final decision on Indonesia's index classification

blocks.text: **What changed and why.** This update answers the 5 November repeat of the price alert, and the answer is only partly tape. The IHSG lost -16.7% in October after MSCI opened its standalone consultation, with -7.0% of that in the last week of the month [S37][S36]; FOLK had already been placed under unusual-market-activity surveillance on 15 October [S4][S28]; and a holder above five per cent has been selling: 25 million shares at 100.0 on 14 October and a further 73.7 million reported on 3 November, cutting the stake to 18.4% [S2][S33]. But those named drivers cover only part of the fall to Rp59, and the 4 November release — cash of IDR9.9bn against IDR11.5bn of liabilities, IDR36.6bn of portfolio sold — lands inside the same window and is at least as plausible a cause as the flow [S34][S0]. We therefore do not attribute the whole sequence to supply; the data pack carries monthly rather than daily closes, so the last five sessions cannot be decomposed [S0].

What the release adds is the composition of the profit, not a new mark. Of IDR26.7bn of net other income, IDR20.1bn was an unrealised fair-value gain, IDR5.0bn a realised investment gain and IDR1.2bn dividend income [S34]. The equity portfolio reached IDR105.4bn, of which IDR57.4bn is listed; cash was only IDR9.9bn, with liabilities of IDR11.5bn, and IDR36.6bn of the portfolio was sold in the quarter to raise cash [S34]. That is a holdco funding itself by selling investments, not one sitting on a cash pile. The nine-month attributable profit of IDR18.4bn is not a post-June step-up — the June balance sheet already contains the first half — so it is no longer carried as a bridge. We rebuild the SOTP from the 30 September balance sheet and reconcile it in the valuation section, and we keep the SELL rating, the Rp26 target and the -55.1% return from Rp59 [S0].

FOLK is a small multi-sector holding that listed in 2023 as a media, retail-brand and intellectual-property group, then recapitalised through a private placement and pivoted into healthcare and infrastructure [S3][S10]. The share price ran from a few dozen rupiah to a four-digit high and has since fallen sharply, leaving a market capitalisation of IDR241.4bn against group equity of IDR140.5bn at 30 September 2026 [S0][S19].

The variant view is simple and uncomfortable: the data-centre exposure that the market is paying for is not a data-centre business. FOLK's infrastructure arm, Traya Hydro, supplies water and wastewater treatment to two large projects in the Cikarang cluster, and the company explicitly declines to disclose the contract value or the identity of the developers [S6]. The cluster itself is large, with announced investment above 6 billion and planned capacity above 600 MW, but those are the developers' numbers, not FOLK's order book [S6]. We still cannot find a contract value, margin or term for Traya in the public record; the only hard number is the revenue it has started to contribute, which we now use as a run-rate mark [S19].

What moves the value is therefore not a data-centre multiple but three marked parts and one deduction: the IDR105.4bn equity portfolio, including the listed Diagnos stake marked at the 27 October close; Traya's consolidated revenue run-rate; the book residual of the media, retail and IP estate, which is not an independent mark; and a net holdco deduction that replaces the June net cash, because at 30 September cash of IDR9.9bn sat against IDR11.5bn of liabilities before capitalised overhead [S0][S16][S34]. The first is marked by the market; the second is a run-rate mark, not a contract; the third is a loss-making estate carried at book because there is no better source; the deduction reflects a parent that funded its quarter by selling investments. The only bridge item is a probability-weighted reversal of the unrealised gain, because the gain is reported but not realised. At Rp59 the shares still change hands above a post-discount SOTP of Rp24 per share [S0][S4]. A reader who wants the bull case should read the scenario section: it requires a disclosed contract with a sourceable value and a named corporate action, neither of which exists today.

FOLK describes itself as a multi-sector investment holding listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, rooted in new media, retail brands and intellectual property and now expanding into healthcare, mining and resources, and utility infrastructure [S10]. The legacy operating estate includes the digital media platform Folkative, the media and content assets USS Networks and Finfolk, the fashion brand Amazara, the hygiene brand Dr. Soap and the make-up brand Syca [S9][S14]. These are small consumer and media businesses, not a scaled platform; the group employed only 38 people at the last disclosure [S0]. The company describes its approach as active stewardship and disciplined capital allocation, but the operating footprint remains small, Jakarta-based and concentrated in a handful of brands [S10].

The strategy changed after the January 2026 private placement, which brought in roughly IDR54.0bn of share premium and took the share count to about four thousand million shares [S3]. Management then acquired 99.96 per cent of Traya Multi Investama for a nominal consideration, gaining control of Traya Hydro, a water technology company that provides integrated water and wastewater treatment through membrane filtration systems [S5][S12]. In May 2026 FOLK subscribed to new Diagnos shares in a private placement, taking a stake in the listed clinical-laboratory operator [S11][S13]. The company frames this as a shift from a creative-consumer ecosystem to a diversified investment platform [S3].

The group structure is a listed parent over unlisted operating subsidiaries plus a minority stake in a listed healthcare company. Traya Hydro is owned 99.9 per cent through the Traya Multi Investama vehicle, which FOLK acquired for IDR0.2bn [S5][S6]. Diagnos is listed under DGNS, and FOLK bought 95 million new shares at 269.0, a total investment of IDR25.6bn [S11]. Sumber Garam Pratama held 825 million shares after selling a block in October 2026, and a 3 November summary puts its stake at 18.4% after a further sale of 73.7 million shares [S2][S33]. The data pack's free-float and insider percentages are dated 4 November but reflect the register before that 3 November block; adjusted for it, the free float is nearer a third and the insider block lower, both still comfortably above the exchange minimum [S0][S17]. The filings we hold do not name a single controlling shareholder and do not rank holders, so we describe Sumber Garam Pratama only as a declared holder rather than assert control.

The ownership picture matters because the group's expansion has been funded by equity issued to new investors rather than by operating cash flow [S3]. The company's own investor-relations page lists annual reports, quarterly financial information and shareholder meetings, but the links currently resolve to a placeholder test document rather than to filed accounts, so a public investor cannot read the audited annual report from the company website [S10]. That is a transparency gap we treat as a governance flag, not a data inconvenience; it is also why the parent-only cost split and the Q2-Q3 non-operating items cannot be verified.

FOLK sits in the IDX-IC conglomerates bucket, but its economics are those of a tiny diversified holding rather than a scaled industrial group. The relevant sub-markets are Indonesian digital media and consumer brands, clinical diagnostics, and water and wastewater treatment for industrial and data-centre customers [S10][S12][S13]. Each is competitive and none is a natural monopoly. The media properties compete for audience and advertising with far larger platforms, the consumer brands compete on shelf space and online acquisition cost, and the water-treatment business competes for engineering, procurement and construction contracts against established plant suppliers.

The data-centre cluster is the only part of the story with visible external momentum. The Cikarang area has become Indonesia's largest data-centre development cluster, with developers announcing investment above 6 billion and combined capacity above 600 MW, and potential expansion toward a gigawatt [S6]. That is a genuine demand driver for water treatment, cooling and wastewater services. However, the value capture depends on contract terms, pricing and the ability to execute multiple projects simultaneously, and FOLK discloses none of these for Traya [S6].

Regulation and market structure are two-sided. On the one hand, Indonesia's digital and healthcare demand is growing with GDP, and the macro deck has real GDP growth of 5.3 per cent for FY2027E, which supports advertising, diagnostics and infrastructure spending [S0]. On the other hand, the exchange is removing high-shareholding-concentration names from the IHSG calculation from 2 November 2026 [S17], and MSCI opened a consultation on 15 October 2026 to reclassify Indonesia from Emerging to Standalone, with feedback to 30 April 2027 and a decision by 30 June 2027 [S18]. FOLK itself is not on the published HSC list and its free float, on the register before the November block, is 31.3%, comfortably above the exchange minimum [S0][S17], so the direct index risk is market-wide rather than name-specific; it still reduces the passive bid for small, concentrated holdings.

The moat assessment is weak. Traya Hydro's membrane technology is differentiated at the project level but not proprietary in a way that protects pricing; the media brands have audience relationships but no durable pricing power; and the healthcare stake is a minority position with no control [S11][S12][S13]. Five-forces pressure is high from suppliers of membrane equipment and from rival engineering firms, high from buyers who can multi-source water treatment, moderate from new entrants in media, and low from substitutes in diagnostics. The one structural advantage is the unlevered balance sheet and the liquid listed portfolio, which let the parent bid for small projects without balance-sheet stress [S3][S34]. In water treatment specifically, the customer relationship is project-based and lumpy, so a single large contract can flatter one year of revenue without creating recurring earnings [S6][S12].

For a holding company, the industry question is less about any single segment and more about whether the centre allocates capital well. The record so far is a sequence of small related-party and negotiated transactions rather than a demonstrated ability to buy assets cheaply and upstream cash [S5][S11][S10]. We therefore treat the conglomerate structure as a discount factor, consistent with the house holdco method, rather than as a source of synergy value.

The reported history is one of shrinkage and losses. Revenue fell from IDR40.2bn in FY2022 to IDR24.8bn, IDR19.4bn and IDR18.8bn in the following years, while gross profit recovered only because the low-margin retail business was wound down [S0]. Operating costs did not shrink with the top line: SG&A was IDR23.4bn against gross profit of IDR9.8bn, producing an EBIT loss of IDR-13.6bn and an EBITDA loss of IDR-9.6bn [S0]. The company reports that operating expenses changed -22.4% in 2025, which is directionally helpful but not enough to close the gap at the current revenue base [S3].

The first three quarters of 2026 are dominated by non-operating items rather than by an operating turnaround. FOLK reported a net profit of IDR14.8bn in Q1 2026, its first profit since listing, but the operating line was still negative and the profit came from below EBIT [S0][S3]. In Q2 2026 the sign reversed: the company reported a net loss while operating EBIT remained negative, and the swing below EBIT accounted for essentially all of it [S0]. In Q3 the sign reversed again: the company reports IDR20.4bn of group net profit on IDR5.1bn of revenue, taking the nine-month attributable profit to IDR18.4bn and nine-month basic EPS to 4.5 [S19][S20]. Note that the quarterly figure is group net profit, while the nine-month figure is the portion attributable to the parent, because minorities carried a small loss [S20].

The Q3 composition is disclosed in the 5 November account, and it is a mark-to-market result rather than an operating one. Net other income of IDR26.7bn comprised a IDR20.1bn unrealised fair-value gain, IDR5.0bn of realised investment gains and IDR1.2bn of dividends [S34]. The unrealised gain alone accounts for virtually all of the IDR20.4bn Q3 group profit, and it is struck below EBIT [S34][S20]. A Diagnos mark-up cannot explain it: the stake is 95 million shares and the May placement price was 269.0 against a 288.0 close, so the whole mark-up is a fraction of the gain [S11][S16]. The gain is instead a revaluation of the wider equity portfolio, which reached IDR105.4bn at 30 September, of which IDR57.4bn is listed [S34]. The portfolio is carried at fair value inside equity, so the valuation now takes that mark directly rather than rebuilding it from a June base; what is not known is whether the gain repeats or reverses, and that is why the bridge carries a probability-weighted reversal rather than the nine-month profit. No Q2 or Q3 2026 LK is archived and the IR site serves a placeholder, so the composition is a company statement rather than a full reconciliation [S10].

The balance sheet is liquid rather than cash-heavy. The January placement added IDR54.0bn of share premium, total equity rose to IDR137.8bn by March 2026, total assets reached IDR147.5bn, and liabilities were only IDR9.7bn with no bank debt [S3]. By September, group equity was IDR140.5bn and total assets IDR152.0bn, still with no bank loans [S19]. The 5 November account puts September cash at IDR9.9bn against liabilities of IDR11.5bn: the June cash balance has been redeployed into the IDR105.4bn equity portfolio, IDR57.4bn of it listed, and IDR36.6bn of cash was realised from partial portfolio sales in the quarter [S34][S0]. The group is therefore unlevered but no longer cash-funded at the parent: the asset that supports the equity is a marked portfolio, not a cash pile, which is why we carry the portfolio at its reported fair value and do not add cash separately. We found no disclosure of a major asset sale after the balance-sheet date, which is not the same as proof that none occurred [S19][S2][S33]. The portfolio and the absence of debt are the main reasons we do not value the equity at zero. It is also why the market's valuation is still difficult to justify: an unlevered holding whose IDR105.4bn portfolio is marked at fair value trades at IDR241.4bn, above its own reported equity [S0][S19][S34].

Our forecast holds the operating run-rate rather than assuming a rescue. Revenue grows 2% in FY2026E and 5% a year thereafter, gross margin stays near 52%, and SG&A is held at the Q2 2026 observed ratio of 96% of revenue, the last measured quarter in the data pack, rather than rounded up [S0]. D&A is held at the FY2025 actual 21% of revenue rather than the lower FY2024 ratio, so the EBIT line is not flattered by a falling charge [S0]. On those assumptions EBITDA remains negative through the forecast, at IDR-4.3bn in FY2026E. This is an operating-basis forecast: revenue, gross margin, SG&A, D&A and tax only, with every below-EBIT item set to zero, so its negative parent net profit is not an as-reported year and does not contradict the IDR18.4bn nine-month attributable profit the company has already printed [S19][S20]. The forecast balance sheet is an operating roll only and does not capitalise the January placement proceeds, so its equity and net-debt lines are not a forecast of the reported balance sheet and we do not use a forecast-book multiple anywhere in this report. The valuation rests on the 30 September balance sheet below — the IDR105.4bn portfolio, cash of IDR9.9bn, the book residual and the net holdco deduction — not on the forecast roll [S0][S19][S34].

Earnings quality is poor on several measures. The accruals picture is distorted by negative working capital and by the retail wind-down, and cash flow from operations was negative in FY2025, so reported losses are not being flattered by working-capital releases [S0]. The larger flag is that all of the reported profit is struck below EBIT and is non-cash: Q3 alone contributed IDR20.4bn against revenue of IDR5.1bn, the nine-month attributable figure is IDR18.4bn, and the balance-sheet step-up is the same order of magnitude [S19][S20]. That is an accruals-class flag, not a cash-generation story: the profit is larger than the revenue that produced it, so it cannot be a margin on operations, and the IDR20.1bn unrealised fair-value gain is the largest single component of it [S34]. We carry the step-up in the bridge because it is reported equity, not because we can verify it, and we do not treat it as recurring. Related-party gravity is present: the Traya acquisition was a nominal transaction with the controlling director retaining a residual share, and the group's expansion is being executed through negotiated transactions rather than open tenders [S5][S10]. We classify these as optics-class and structure flags, not as evidence of fabricated cash, but they are why the residual book floor is labelled a floor and why the Q3 uplift is shown separately rather than folded into it.

Capital allocation has been equity-funded and acquisition-led. The company raised fresh equity, bought a nominal stake in Traya, subscribed to a Diagnos placement and is now funding working capital for water-treatment projects [S3][S11][S6]. It has never paid a dividend, and the payout assumption is therefore zero [S0]. Until the operating businesses generate free cash flow, the holding depends on the placement proceeds and on the controlling shareholder's willingness to keep supporting it, which is a weaker form of financial flexibility than internally generated cash.

We value FOLK on a sum of the parts because the company is a holding with no single homogeneous earnings stream and because its listed stake, its unlisted operating estate and its cash can each be identified [S0][S16]. The house method for conglomerates is SOTP with honest marks: listed stakes at market value, unlisted segments at book or a sourced metric, less holdco net debt, less holdco overhead capitalised at about ten times, less a holding-company discount anchored to the base rate [S0]. We do not use P/E because the trailing profit is a below-EBIT accounting result and forecast parent earnings are negative, and we do not use the own-history P/BV multiple because the FY2025 observation is contaminated by the squeeze to a four-digit share price [S0][S19].

The parts are rebuilt at 30 September 2026. The equity portfolio is marked at its reported fair value of IDR105.4bn, of which IDR57.4bn is listed [S34]; that figure includes the Diagnos stake, so the old practice of adding DGNS separately is gone and the double count with it. Traya Hydro is marked at one times the annualised Q3-2026 incremental revenue run-rate. The Q3 release says revenue of IDR5.1bn grew 36.7% year on year and was supported by the Traya water-filter segment; the segment split is not disclosed, so the mark assumes the whole increment is Traya's, which is the generous reading of "supported" [S19]. The media, retail-brand and IP estate has no independent mark. We carry it at the parent-basis book residual after the portfolio, cash and Traya at acquisition cost; that residual embeds every other asset and liability, including the negative minority deficit, and it is a little over a quarter of the gross parts and about three tenths of NAV. It is a book floor, not a valuation, and it is the weakest row in the build.

The Cikarang option is not booked, but it is not ignored. The cluster carries 6 billion dollars of announced developer investment and 600 MW of planned capacity, and water treatment is typically a small percentage of data-centre capex [S6]. A hypothetical capture of one per cent of that programme would be worth several times the entire pre-discount NAV; a tenth of one per cent would be comparable to it. Those are illustrations, not marks: no contract value, term, margin or counterparty is disclosed, and Traya's current revenue is a single quarter's run-rate whose segment split is unknown [S6][S19]. We keep the option out of the SOTP and size it here so the reader can judge what the market is paying for.

The old build started from June parent equity, added the June cash balance and a nine-month profit bridge. That was wrong on the period, not just the arithmetic: the June balance sheet already contains the first half, so the nine-month figure is not a post-June increment, and the June cash had been redeployed into the portfolio by September. The reconciliation is clean. June group equity — parent equity plus the negative minority balance in the data pack — plus the Q3 group profit of IDR20.4bn equals the reported September group equity of IDR140.5bn to within rounding [S0][S20][S19]. The post-June increment is therefore the Q3 result only, and the nine-month attributable figure is not used anywhere in the SOTP. On the parent basis September equity is higher than the group figure by the minority deficit; we use the parent basis consistently for the residual and for the book cross-check, and we show the group figure where the company reports it.

The cost of equity is 11.9% and the WACC is 11.9%, reflecting a 0.90 levered beta, the mature-market risk-free rate and the Indonesia country premium in the house build [S0]. Because the company has no debt, the WACC equals the cost of equity and the discount rate is not the source of the valuation gap. The gap comes from the asset marks and from the holdco discount.

The deduction replaces June net cash. At 30 September cash was IDR9.9bn against IDR11.5bn of liabilities and no bank loans [S34], so the parent is no longer net cash. We add capitalised overhead of about ten times a minimum annual estimate equal to roughly a tenth of the annualised Q2 consolidated SG&A, because no parent-only cost line is published and capitalising the whole consolidated SG&A would double-count the subsidiaries already inside the book residual [S0]. The result is a net deduction, not an addition. It is the optimistic end of the overhead range: a peer-like carry of about twice that amount would reduce the target by roughly an eighth. This is an irreducible evidence gap — the IR site serves a placeholder and no audited LK is retrievable — and it is disclosed rather than hidden [S10].

The only bridge item is the unrealised gain. The IDR20.1bn fair-value gain is reported equity but not cash, and we cannot verify that it repeats; we therefore carry a probability-weighted reversal at one in five, subtracting one fifth of the gain from NAV. The one-in-five basis is a judgement, stated as a judgement rather than a sourced probability. We do not add the realised gains or the dividends: they are already inside the portfolio and the cash line [S34].

We apply a holdco discount at the mid-point of the house base-rate range, because FOLK has no debt and a marked portfolio but also no dividend, a concentrated register, a related-party acquisition record, no dated catalyst to narrow the discount and a holder above five per cent that is still selling down [S2][S10][S33][S34]. FOLK is not on the published HSC list, so HSC exclusion is not a factor in the discount and the earlier draft was wrong to cite it [S17]. The discount is applied to the whole SOTP in the engine, including the portfolio and the net deduction. That is the convention, not a claim that a marked portfolio deserves a holdco discount: if the portfolio were added undiscounted and only the operating residual discounted, the value would be higher, which is a cross-check we state rather than adopt because the marks themselves are the larger uncertainty [S0]. That produces an asset value of Rp24 per share. The published target of Rp26 is that value rolled forward one year at the cost of equity, the engine's standard twelve-month convention. We now lead with the unrolled figure and treat the roll-forward as a convention, because it adds about an eighth to an asset base whose own FY2026E ROE is negative and whose cash yields far less than the cost of equity; it flatters rather than understates [S0]. The target is not a liquidation value: it assumes the operating estate is worth its book residual, Traya is worth its run-rate and the portfolio is worth its reported fair value. Even on those marks the equity is worth a fraction of the current price.

The sensitivity table shows the target across holdco-discount and cost-of-equity steps. The discount dominates: a ten-percentage-point change in the discount moves the value by roughly a tenth of the gross asset base, while a fifty-basis-point change in the cost of equity barely moves it, because the SOTP is an asset valuation rather than a discounted earnings stream [S0]. The engine's reverse DCF cannot bracket today's price: no discount inside the plausible range, nor its complement, brings the pre-discount SOTP up to the market capitalisation, so the implied value is an out-of-range extrapolation rather than a solved discount.

We therefore state the gap attribution as an assumption rather than a measurement. Even after the fall to Rp59, the market capitalisation of IDR241.4bn is above the pre-discount net asset value of these marks, before the 30% holdco discount is applied [S0]. Under (a), the residual estate is at book and every other part is marked, so the whole pre-discount gap is an implied Traya option. Capitalising a water-treatment contractor at ten times earnings on a fifteen per cent net margin, that option implies contract revenue several times the group's entire IDR18.8bn FY2025 revenue, before execution, financing or the confidentiality the company imposes [S6]. Under (b), the residual is marked at one times its own revenue rather than at book; pre-discount NAV falls by the difference and the implied Traya option rises by the same amount. The variant depends on (a): if the market is instead paying above book for the media and IP estate, the implied Traya option falls. We use (a) because the residual has no independent mark and a loss-making estate does not obviously deserve one times revenue. That is the testable version of the variant view: on the most favourable defensible marks, the market is still not paying for the business FOLK owns; it is prepaying a contract FOLK has not disclosed.

We cross-check the SOTP against the market's own marks. The SOTP is built on parent-basis equity; at 30 September the parent figure is the reported group equity of IDR140.5bn plus the minority deficit, so it is the higher of the two and we use it for both the residual and this cross-check [S19]. On that basis the market capitalisation of IDR241.4bn is still above book, so the shares trade at a premium to the equity we actually value, not merely to the group figure [S0][S19]. We deliberately do not use a forecast-book multiple: the engine prints one, but it is struck on a forecast balance sheet that does not capitalise the January placement and is therefore not comparable to the reported accounts. The trailing P/E is not usable because the last twelve months' parent earnings are still negative after the Q2 charge, even though the nine-month 2026 figure is positive; the absence of a clean earnings multiple is itself informative, because a company that cannot be valued on a normalised earnings stream must be valued on assets, and its assets do not support the price [S0][S19].

The downside risks are governance, disclosure and liquidity, in that order. The October tape was market-wide as well as name-specific: the IHSG fell -16.7% in the month on the MSCI consultation and -7.0% in the final week, so part of FOLK's move is beta to a small-cap selloff rather than company news [S37][S36]. The anchor shareholder sold a block in October 2026 at a price well above the current market, and a 3 November summary says it sold a further 73.7 million shares, leaving 18.4% [S2][S33]. On the limited disclosure available — the summary gives no transaction date or price — we read the November item as supply rather than as a signal about the holder's view of value, but we cannot rule the latter out [S33]. The stock was placed on the exchange's unusual-market-activity watchlist after a sharp move, which raises the risk of trading restrictions and of a regulatory request for explanation [S4]. The free float on the register before the November block is 31.3%, comfortably above the exchange minimum and not a name-specific index risk [S0][S17]; the index risk that matters is the market-wide MSCI consultation [S18]. The stock is also outside the fund's minimum-size universe: market capitalisation is IDR241.4bn, below the house floor, while average daily traded value of IDR6.2bn and the main-board listing pass [S0]. The position would have to be sized accordingly.

Macro risk is moderate. A weaker rupiah and higher domestic rates would raise the discount rate and reduce the value of the unlisted estate, while a stronger dollar would help the data-centre investment case at the margin by making the cluster more attractive to international developers [S0]. Commodity and currency exposure is indirect: FOLK does not produce commodities, but its water-treatment projects are priced in rupiah while some equipment is imported, so a weaker currency squeezes project margins. Operational risk is concentrated in Traya's ability to execute multiple projects with a small balance sheet and no disclosed contract terms [S6].

Liquidity is a separate constraint. Average daily traded value is IDR6.2bn, which is adequate for a small position but thin relative to the market capitalisation, and the unusual-market-activity notice shows how quickly the tape can become disorderly [S0][S4]. For a fund, the exit is the risk, not only the valuation.

The bear case assumes the data-centre story stays unquantified, the unrealised gain reverses, the anchor keeps selling and the discount widens to the top of the house range. It also carries the funding risk explicitly: with cash of IDR9.9bn against IDR11.5bn of liabilities, a negative EBITDA run-rate and IDR36.6bn of the portfolio already sold to raise cash, the parent has to fund itself [S34]. A placement sized to the cash shortfall plus a year's burn, at a thirty per cent discount to the post-discount SOTP, would add about a tenth to the share count and take the twelve-month target to the mid-twenties; a forced sale of the listed sleeve at a fifth below market would remove about a twelfth of NAV. The base case assumes the book residual holds, the portfolio keeps its reported fair value, Traya's revenue run-rate persists and the discount stays at the mid-point. The bull case assumes a disclosed water-treatment contract with a sourceable value and a discount at the bottom of the range; because no value is disclosed, the contract is an option we size rather than book. Probabilities are 25% bear, 50% base and 25% bull, with a mirrored discount shock in the engine [S0].

The engine's scenario shocks move model inputs, and the SOTP marks are fixed rows, so the table's bear widens the discount but cannot write the residual or the portfolio down. The true downside cases are therefore shown as a memo, not as a fourth scenario, and they are computed against the stated pre-discount NAV. The operating residual is about three tenths of that NAV: halving it removes about a seventh of NAV and, on the wide-end discount, takes the twelve-month target into the low twenties; a full write-down leaves a target at about a third of today's price. The portfolio is about three quarters of pre-discount NAV: a thirty per cent fall removes about a fifth, and a fifty per cent fall about two fifths. The stated bear is the top of the discount range on the marks we can defend, not the worst case; the book-stress and funding cases are below it [S0][S16][S19][S34].

One further risk is that the holding structure itself becomes the story. If management uses the post-placement balance sheet for further negotiated acquisitions in healthcare or infrastructure, the discount should widen rather than narrow, because each transaction adds a new related-party mark that minority holders cannot independently value [S5][S11]. The reverse is also possible: a clean, arm's-length purchase of a cash-generating asset at a disclosed price would be the first evidence that the centre can allocate capital well, and we would raise the marks accordingly [S10].

The signposts that would change our view are specific. A contract announcement with a value, term and counterparty for Traya Hydro would move the infrastructure asset from a run-rate mark to a cash-flow mark; we would need the contract value and margin to underwrite it [S6]. A dividend or a buyback at the holdco level would be evidence that cash can be upstreamed; today there is none [S10]. A sale of the Diagnos stake at a premium to its 27 October market price would validate the listed mark [S16]. Conversely, a further related-party acquisition, a new share issue or a fresh block sale would widen the discount and validate the bear case [S2].

Ownership is concentrated. The data pack shows insiders holding 68.1% of the register and a free float of 31.3%, but those figures are dated 4 November and reflect the register before the 3 November block; adjusted for the 73.7 million shares sold, the free float is nearer a third and Sumber Garam Pratama's reported stake is 18.4% [S0][S2][S33]. The filings we hold do not name a single controlling shareholder, so we do not assert one. FOLK is not on the published high-shareholding-concentration list, so HSC exclusion is not a governance or discount factor for this name [S17]; its free float is above the exchange minimum [S0]; the exchange is removing HSC names from the IHSG from 2 November 2026 [S17], and MSCI's standalone consultation is market-wide [S18]. None of that is a finding of wrongdoing, but concentration, the related-party record and the disclosure gap change the investor base and the liquidity profile.

Related-party dealings are a live issue. The Traya Multi Investama acquisition left the president director with a residual single share of the target, and the group's expansion into healthcare and infrastructure has been executed through negotiated transactions rather than open tenders [S5][S10]. The company's investor-relations page lists annual reports and quarterly information but currently serves a placeholder document, so the audited accounts are not readily available from the company website [S10]. We could not verify the auditor, the audit opinion, the board committees, the parent-only cost split or the Q2-Q3 2026 non-operating items from a company filing in this window. Those are irreducible evidence gaps, stated as gaps rather than papered over with an assumed number.

The dividend record is empty: no dividend has been paid since the 2023 listing, and the payout assumption is zero [S0]. The board is young and small, with a president director whose background is in venture capital and financial services and commissioners drawn from property and consumer businesses [S10]. We see no evidence of pledged controlling shares in the public record we reviewed, but the absence of a filing-level disclosure means we cannot rule it out.

ESG exposure is modest at the group level but specific at the asset level. The water-treatment business has a positive environmental rationale because it improves industrial water reuse and wastewater quality, and the data-centre cluster's water demand is a genuine sustainability issue [S6][S12]. The media and consumer brands have limited direct environmental footprint. The main social and governance issues are disclosure quality, related-party transacting and the concentration of ownership. Those are the factors we weigh inside the holdco-discount range; the absence of debt and the liquid portfolio offset them, so we apply the mid-point rather than the wide end, and the residual book floor we carry is the generous side of the asset marks [S2][S10].

Q3 2026 has now printed: revenue of IDR5.1bn and nine-month attributable profit of IDR18.4bn, with Traya consolidated from April 2026 [S19][S20]. The release still discloses no contract value, margin or backlog for Traya, so the infrastructure asset is marked on its revenue run-rate, not on a contract [S6][S19]. The next dated checkpoint is the FY2026 audited accounts in the statutory window to 31 March 2027 — a nine-month Traya consolidation, because April is the first consolidated month, so FY2027 is the first full year — and it is the first test of whether the reported profit converts to cash. The deadline is general regulatory knowledge (the OJK annual-report rule), not a company-sourced date, and we do not cite the Q3 release for it. The MSCI consultation takes feedback to 30 April 2027 and a decision by 30 June 2027, which will determine whether the passive bid for small Indonesian holdings improves or deteriorates [S18]. The exchange's removal of HSC names from the IHSG takes effect on 2 November 2026, but FOLK is not on the list, so it is a market-wide rather than a name-specific event [S17].

Between updates we monitor five KPIs: the September cash line of IDR9.9bn and the IDR105.4bn portfolio mark, including the IDR57.4bn listed sleeve [S34]; the EBITDA loss and whether SG&A stays near the Q2 2026 run-rate [S0]; the composition of the below-EBIT profit and whether the IDR20.1bn fair-value gain repeats or reverses [S34][S20]; any disclosed contract value or backlog at Traya Hydro [S6]; and the size and price of any further anchor-shareholder sales [S2][S33]. We also monitor the Diagnos stake at its 27 October market price against the IDR25.6bn cost, because a mark-to-market move changes the SOTP [S16][S11].

Holding companies in emerging markets often trade below the sum of their parts because minority shareholders cannot force the sale of assets or the upstreaming of cash. The discount tends to narrow only when a controller chooses to act, and it widens when related-party transactions or opaque disclosure raise the cost of trust. That is the framework we apply here rather than treating a low multiple as an automatic opportunity.

bear.narrative: The data-centre story stays unquantified, the unrealised fair-value gain reverses, the >5% anchor keeps selling, and the market applies the wide end of the holdco range. The funding bear is explicit: with cash of Rp9.94bn against Rp11.52bn of liabilities and a forecast EBITDA loss, a placement of roughly Rp7bn at a 30% discount to the post-discount SOTP would add about a tenth to the share count and take the twelve-month target to the mid-twenties; a forced sale of the listed sleeve at a fifth below market would remove about a twelfth of NAV. The engine's shock moves only the discount because the SOTP rows are fixed marks; the memo stress in section 5 halves and writes off the operating residual and marks the portfolio down, and those are the true downside cases. A half write-down of the operating residual removes about a quarter of pre-discount NAV; a full write-down leaves about a fifth of today's price.

bull.narrative: The portfolio is already marked at fair value and Traya at its annualised run-rate; a disclosed water-treatment contract with a sourceable value would add an option the SOTP still does not carry. The Cikarang cluster carries USD6bn of announced developer investment and 600MW of capacity; at a hypothetical one per cent capture the contract value would be several times the entire pre-discount NAV, and even a tenth of one per cent would be comparable to it. We do not book the option because no contract value, term, margin or counterparty is disclosed and Traya's current revenue is a single quarter's run-rate. With the marks fixed, the only quantified engine lever is the discount narrowing to the bottom of the house range.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2025 revenue was Rp18.8bn and H1-26 runs at about Rp19bn annualised; the media/retail/IP base is mature while Traya Multi Investama consolidates from April 2026, but no contract values are disclosed, so growth is held near nominal GDP after a flat 2026 [S0][S6].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2025 gross margin was 52% and H1-26 about 51%; held at 52% as water treatment and healthcare services enter the mix [S0][S6].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 SG&A was 125% of revenue; the last observed quarter (Q2-26) was 95.7% (5.037/5.262) per the data pack, and the company disclosed a 22.4% FY2025 opex cut [S0][S3]. The base case holds the observed 95.7% flat rather than rounding up to 100%; EBIT stays negative through the forecast [S0].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 actual ratio of 21% of revenue (Rp3.93bn on Rp18.76bn), the last audited year, rather than the lower FY2024 ratio [S0]. A higher D&A charge lowers EBIT and leaves EBITDA unchanged; group D&A was not restated in the pack because the LK notes could not be retrieved.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex was 0.6% and FY2024 1.3% of revenue; the media estate is capital-light and 2% covers maintenance plus small water-treatment equipment [S0][S12].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was negative at 12% of revenue after the retail wind-down; held near zero [S0].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The group is loss-making and the LK shows only minor tax credits, so no cash tax is modelled [S0].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FOLK had no bank debt at Q1-26 and the Q2-26 pack shows zero debt [S3][S0].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: The model's opening cash is the FY2025 reported balance; 5.5% approximates the IDR time-deposit rate in the macro deck [S0].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No debt and no funded expansion plan disclosed, so net borrowing is zero [S0][S3].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Set to zero: the model is an OPERATING-BASIS forecast (revenue, gross margin, SG&A, D&A, tax only) and deliberately excludes every below-EBIT item. The company has already reported 9M attributable profit of Rp18.40bn, which the report shows as reported; it is not an FY2026E forecast [S19][S20][S0].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities absorbed 27% of the FY2025 loss (a negative minority balance), so 27% is carried forward [S0].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend has been paid since the 2023 listing and the company is investing its placement proceeds, so payout stays at zero [S0][S10].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Shares rose to 4,091mn after the January 2026 placement (3,948mn at FY2025), a 3.6% increase; no further issue is approved [S0][S3].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for IDR, below the 5.29% FY2027E real GDP path in the macro deck [S0].

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: House base rate for holdco discounts is 20-40%; FOLK sits at the mid-point because it has no bank debt and a marked portfolio, offset by no dividend, a concentrated register, related-party acquisitions, a thin liquidity position at 30 September (cash Rp9.94bn against Rp11.52bn of liabilities), no dated narrowing catalyst and a >5% anchor that is still selling down [S2][S10][S33][S34]. FOLK is NOT on the published HSC list and that is not a discount-widening factor [S17]. The discount is applied to the whole SOTP in the engine; the report shows the portfolio-undiscounted cross-check.

challenges.challenge: The bridge adds the nine-month attributable profit (F23, Rp18.40bn) to a 30 June parent-equity base (Rp136.00bn [S0]) and calls it the "Q3-2026 attributable profit ... after the June balance sheet". A June balance sheet already contains Q1. The post-June parent increment is either the Q3 attributable figure (Rp20.35bn group, F27, which the report's own "minorities carried a small loss" reading implies) or as little as Rp3.58bn if Q1's Rp14.82bn (F1) is inside the June base; the record cannot distinguish the two without the Q3 LK, and the two readings differ by about Rp14.8bn, or a tenth of the target. The claim that "rebuilding the SOTP from the September balance sheet gives the same total as the June build plus the bridge" is therefore unproven.
challenges.answer: Rebuilt the SOTP on 30 September 2026 and removed the nine-month profit from the bridge. The reconciliation is June group equity (parent 136.00 plus the negative minority balance of 15.88 in the data pack) plus the Q3 group profit of 20.35 equals the reported September group equity of 140.46 to within rounding, so the June base already contains Q1 and Q2 and the post-June increment is the Q3 result only, not 18.40 and not 3.58. The nine-month attributable figure is not used anywhere in the SOTP.

challenges.challenge: The largest SOTP row (Rp64.74bn, 46% of gross parts and 55% of NAV) is not a mark. It is June parent equity Rp136.00bn less June cash Rp45.36bn less DGNS at cost Rp25.65bn less Traya at cost Rp0.25bn, and it is labelled "Media, retail brands and IP". Inside that row sits the entire non-DGNS equity portfolio, which at 30 September was Rp105.44bn in total, Rp57.37bn of it listed [S34]. The report itself calls the row a floor and "an upper bound on what a buyer would pay", which is not a valuation of the media business; the holdco card requires each holding at a house or appropriate mark, not a book plug.
challenges.answer: Split the row. The equity portfolio is now a mark at 30 September fair value of Rp105.44bn, of which Rp57.37bn is listed, and the operating media/retail/IP estate is carried separately at the parent-basis book residual after that portfolio, cash and Traya at acquisition cost. The residual is labelled a book floor, not a mark, and the report states its size as a share of gross parts and NAV. The double count with DGNS is removed because the stake sits inside the portfolio figure.

challenges.challenge: The price-move attribution is asserted at the magnitude that matters. The sources support the market-wide part (IHSG -16.7% in October [S37], -7.03% in the final week [S36]) and two block sales (25mn at Rp100 on 14 October [S2]; a 73.65mn headline on 3 November [S33]), but those explain roughly 7pp of a 24pp five-day fall, and the 3 November item has no date or price. The stock had already fallen 74.2% year-to-date by 15 October [S4], so most of the decline predates the October index shock. Meanwhile the 4 November release disclosing cash at Rp9.94bn against Rp11.52bn of liabilities and Rp36.59bn of portfolio sold [S34] falls inside the same window and is dismissed without a test.
challenges.answer: The data pack carries monthly closes only (2026-09 184, 2026-10 64, 2026-11 59), not daily closes or turnover for 29 October to 5 November, so the five-session fall cannot be decomposed against the index and the block. We have stopped attributing the whole move to flow: the report now says the named drivers cover only part of the fall, treats the 4 November release (cash 9.94 against liabilities 11.52, Rp36.59bn of portfolio sold) as at least as plausible a cause as the flow, and states that the sessions cannot be separated. The 3 November item is cited as a headline with no date or price.

challenges.challenge: The September disclosure changes the funding profile and the update does not carry it. Cash is Rp9.94bn against Rp11.52bn of liabilities, FY2026E EBITDA is -Rp5.2bn, no dividend has ever been paid, and the parent funded the quarter by selling Rp36.59bn of investments [S34][S0]. That is a holdco liquidating its own portfolio to meet costs, not a holdco with Rp45.36bn of unencumbered cash. A fresh placement at a discount to NAV, or a forced sale of the Rp57.37bn listed sleeve into the same thin tape that is already selling, is a per-share dilution and a discount-widening event that neither the base case nor the bear case contains.
challenges.answer: Added a funding bear inside the bear narrative and the risk section: cash Rp9.94bn against liabilities Rp11.52bn, negative EBITDA, and Rp36.59bn of portfolio already sold. A placement sized to the shortfall plus a year's burn at a 30% discount to the post-discount SOTP adds about a tenth to the share count and takes the target to the mid-twenties; a forced sale of the listed sleeve at a fifth below market removes about a twelfth of NAV. The engine shock still moves only the discount because the SOTP rows are fixed marks, so the dilution is quantified in the narrative and memo rather than as a fourth scenario.

challenges.challenge: The update quantifies the bear side of the data-centre option but never the bull side. The Cikarang cluster carries USD6bn of announced developer investment and 600MW, with potential to 1GW [S6]; water treatment is typically a small percentage of data-centre capex, but at even a low-single-digit share the addressable value would exceed the entire NAV. Instead Traya is marked at Rp5.5bn, one times a single quarter's annualised increment, which the report itself calls the bottom of a 1x-to-10x band [S19]. Without an order of magnitude the reader cannot judge whether the market's implied Rp100bn Traya option is absurd or merely early.
challenges.answer: Sized the Cikarang option qualitatively in the report: at a hypothetical one per cent capture of the USD6bn programme the contract value would be several times the pre-discount NAV, and a tenth of one per cent would be comparable to it. The option is not booked because no contract value, term, margin or counterparty is disclosed; Traya stays at one times the annualised Q3 run-rate.

challenges.challenge: The bridge is carried at probability 1.0 (valuation.bridge, F23) although the report states the component is an unrealised fair-value gain of Rp20.07bn on a Rp105.44bn portfolio and that "what is not known is whether it repeats or reverses" [S34]. A reversal removes about Rp3.5 per share of NAV; a 30% fall in the listed sleeve alone removes about Rp2.4. Assigning certainty to the least verifiable asset contradicts the report's own earnings-quality section and the base-case standard that a probability accompanies every bridge item.
challenges.answer: Removed the bridge at certainty. The only bridge item is now a probability-weighted reversal of the Rp20.07bn unrealised fair-value gain at 20%, which subtracts one fifth of the gain from NAV. The basis is stated as a judgement, not a sourced probability, and the report says the gain is reported equity but not cash. The realised gains and dividends are not added because they are already inside the portfolio and cash lines.

challenges.challenge: Traya's Rp5.5bn mark is one times the annualised Q3 revenue increment, which assumes (a) the whole 36.7% growth is Traya and (b) one quarter is a run-rate. S19 says revenue growth was "ditopang kontribusi segmen filter air dari Traya", supported by, not wholly attributable to it, and the segment split is undisclosed. The report also gives a 1x-to-10x band and takes the floor without saying why a business growing 36.7% deserves the floor rather than the middle.
challenges.answer: Traya's Rp5.5bn mark is now stated as an assumption, not a sourced split: one times the annualised Q3 incremental revenue, at the floor of a 1x-10x band, because the segment split is undisclosed and S19 says growth was 'ditopang' (supported), not caused, by the water-filter segment. The report says the mark assumes the whole increment is Traya's and calls that the generous reading. No water-treatment peer multiple was sourced in this window; the evidence gap is stated rather than filled.

challenges.challenge: SG&A is held at 100% of revenue when the Q2-26 observed ratio is 95.7% and the company disclosed a 22.4% operating-expense cut [S3]. The report calls it a "rounded-up hold", which is honest, but the QC justification calls the same number "the observed run-rate", which it is not. The card forbids default haircuts without a source; this one is conservative in the right direction but unsourced.
challenges.answer: Opex is now set to the observed Q2-26 ratio of 95.7% (5.037/5.262) held flat, not rounded to 100%. The assumptions basis and the QC justification both cite the observed ratio and the mix shift; the report no longer calls the 100% figure the observed run-rate.

challenges.challenge: The target is the SOTP rolled forward one year at 11.85%, which adds about Rp2.9 per share (11%) to an asset base with negative ROE and cash yielding 5.5%. FOLK's COE is the lowest in the CONGLOMERATES peer set (eleven peers range 12.6% to 21.2%) and rests on an industry-default 0.90 beta with no small-cap or liquidity premium, even though the report itself calls the stock illiquid and outside the fund's size floor. The roll-forward is disclosed as flattering but kept.
challenges.answer: The report now leads with the unrolled SOTP of Rp23.68 per share and treats the Rp26.48 target as the engine's twelve-month roll-forward convention, stating that the roll adds about an eighth to an asset base with negative FY2026E ROE and cash yielding 5.5%. The COE itself is a house-build output and is not re-underwritten here.

challenges.challenge: The bear memo overstates itself. The residual is Rp64.74bn of Rp141.46bn pre-discount NAV, about 46%, not "about three fifths"; halving it is about 23% of NAV, not "about three tenths"; and a full write-down leaves about 21% of the current price on the wide discount, not "roughly a sixth". Each error makes the downside look larger than the arithmetic supports.
challenges.answer: The memo is recomputed against the rebuilt pre-discount NAV. The operating residual is about three tenths of NAV; halving it removes about a seventh and takes the target into the low twenties; a full write-down leaves a target at about a third of today's price. The portfolio is about three quarters of NAV; a 30% fall removes about a fifth and a 50% fall about two fifths. The earlier three-fifths and one-sixth claims are withdrawn.

challenges.challenge: The "above book" cross-check compares market capitalisation with group equity of Rp140.5bn [S19], while the SOTP is built on parent equity of Rp136.0bn [S0]. With negative minority interest the parent figure is the higher of the two, so the report mixes bases: the premium to book quoted in the text is not the premium to the base it actually values. Small in size, but a reader cannot reconcile the two.
challenges.answer: The report states both bases at 30 September: group equity of Rp140.46bn and parent equity, which is higher by the minority deficit. The SOTP residual and the book cross-check now use the parent basis consistently, and the report says the market cap is above the equity actually valued rather than merely above the group figure.

missing_bull_case.note: The Cikarang option is never sized. USD6bn of developer capex and 600MW of capacity [S6] would exceed the entire NAV at even a low-single-digit water-treatment share, yet Traya is marked at Rp5.5bn (one times one quarter's annualised revenue increment) and the report's own 1x-to-10x band is unexplored [S19]. The report quantifies only the bear side of the same option.

missing_bear_case.note: No funding or dilution bear. Cash is Rp9.94bn against Rp11.52bn of liabilities with FY2026E EBITDA of -Rp5.2bn, and Rp36.59bn of portfolio was already sold to fund the quarter [S34][S0]. A placement at a discount to NAV, or continued forced sales of the Rp57.37bn listed sleeve, dilutes per-share value, and neither the base nor the bear carries it; the bear only widens the discount.

assumption_realism.note: The operating hold is credible (Q2-26 SG&A at 95.7% of revenue, Q3 gross margin 54.4% [S34]), but the marks are not. The largest row is a residual plug, the bridge is a nine-month figure presented as the Q3 step-up, and Traya's Rp5.5bn assumes the entire 36.7% revenue growth increment belongs to Traya when S19 says growth was "ditopang" (supported by) the water-filter segment [S19].

evidence_and_citations.note: Most quotes verify (S2, S4, S6, S16, S17, S18, S19, S23, S34, S37). Failures: S33 is a Bing RSS search page carrying only a Pasardana headline, with no body, transaction date or price; the Rp45.36bn June cash and the approximately -24% five-day move carry no fact id; "attributes the whole revenue increase to Traya" overstates S19's "ditopang kontribusi segmen filter air".

valuation_method_fit.note: The SOTP is parent book plus two mark-ups: June parent equity Rp136.00bn [S0], DGNS cost to market +Rp1.81bn, Traya cost to run-rate +Rp5.25bn, bridge Rp18.40bn, capitalised overhead -Rp20.00bn. The Rp64.74bn residual (46% of gross parts) is a plug, not a mark, and its label misstates the equity portfolio inside it. VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT also requires look-through earnings, dividend-upstream coverage and factor tags; none is present.

bias_and_tone.note: The SELL survives doubling the bear probability, so it is not one-input heroic. But "it is not evidence about the value of the assets" and "we treat the whole sequence as flow" are asserted: the named drivers cover about 7pp of a 24pp fall, and the 4 November release (cash down to Rp9.94bn, Rp20.07bn of the profit unrealised [S34]) lands inside the same window and is not tested as the alternative cause.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: No commodity, royalty or realisation basis applies. The house macro deck (FY2027E GDP 5.29%, USD/IDR 18,350) is read correctly and the 30% holdco discount sits inside the 20-40% base rate. FOLK's 11.85% COE is the lowest of twelve CONGLOMERATES names (12.6% to 21.2%), but it is a house-build output rather than a deck input, so it is raised under C9.

conservatism_audit.note: Two-sided. Conservative: opex rounded up to 100% against 95.7% observed, Traya at one times revenue, overhead at the stated "minimum" Rp20bn, and the 30% discount applied to Rp45.36bn of cash. Optimistic: the Rp18.40bn bridge at probability 1.0, a mid-point discount for a name with no dated catalyst, and the 11.85% COE roll-forward. The bridge alone is worth about Rp3.5 per share if it reverses; the opex hold is worth nothing to the SOTP.

calibration.note: All three flags are answered, but the calibration justification calls the 100% FY+1 opex ratio "the observed run-rate" when the observed Q2-26 ratio is 95.7%: it is a rounded-up hold, which the report itself concedes. The SOTP carries no calibration to reported book, and FY2026E np_parent of -Rp6.65bn still sits against a printed 9M +Rp18.40bn [S19], explained only as an operating-basis forecast.

signoff.notes: APPROVED — leave at signoff for the Director to publish. SELL, target Rp26.48 (unrolled SOTP Rp23.68) is the engine output and the text matches it: portfolio Rp105.44bn at 30-Sep fair value, Traya Rp5.5bn at 1x the annualised Q3 increment, operating residual Rp41.52bn on parent book, cash Rp9.94bn net of Rp20.0bn capitalised overhead, a 20%-weighted FV-reversal bridge, and a 30% discount inside the 20-40% holdco base rate. All six MATERIAL challenges (C1-C6) are answered on substance and the changes are in the files; 0 FATAL. The SELL survives the most generous marks (QC: pre-discount NAV Rp138.4bn against a Rp241.4bn market cap) and the batch is not one-sided (ADD/HOLD/REDUCE/SELL), so there is no shared-input tilt. Clear before the next version: Q1 stale displayed bridge (target unaffected), Q2 state the Rp16.68bn NCI deficit and its ~Rp3.2/share group-basis effect, Q3 bound the Traya book overlap. Q4-Q6 are notes.

bias.note: Every discretionary mark is generous to the target, not bearish: the operating residual is struck on PARENT book (Rp157.15bn, which is group net assets of Rp140.47bn plus the Rp16.68bn negative minority deficit [S0][S19]), overhead is deducted at a stated Rp20.0bn MINIMUM rather than a peer-like carry, the discount is the 30% mid-point although FOLK has no dated catalyst, Traya is one times the run-rate, and the portfolio is carried at the company's full reported fair value with only one fifth of one quarter's unrealised gain reversed. Even on those marks pre-discount NAV of Rp138.4bn sits 43% below the Rp241.4bn market capitalisation, so the SELL survives the most generous inputs; correcting the most generous item (the NCI deficit) still gives about Rp23.3. The 20% FV-reversal is a judgement with no anchor, but it is directionally right and worth 2.9% of NAV.

findings.finding: Judge FIX accepted: the displayed bridge is stale. The packet shows net debt of -45.4 (June cash) and a standalone -15.9 minority deduction, neither of which is in the September SOTP, and the -15.9 row double-reads the minority deficit that the parent-basis residual already embeds. The Rp23.68 SOTP itself reconciles on the September construction, so the target is unaffected.

The residual is struck on parent equity of Rp157.15bn, which exceeds total group net assets of Rp140.47bn by the Rp16.68bn negative minority deficit [S0][S19]. The report states that the parent figure is higher than the group figure but never gives the amount, and it does not say whether the deficit is recoverable; an NCI cannot in law fund a negative balance, so on a group basis the residual falls to Rp24.84bn, NAV to Rp121.7bn and the target to about Rp23.3 (-Rp3.2, -12%). This is the largest single judgement in the build and it is currently disclosed only qualitatively.

Traya is added at Rp5.5bn while its consolidated book net assets remain inside the operating residual: only the Rp0.25bn acquisition cost is removed from parent equity, not the subsidiary's book equity, so the same asset is counted at book and again at one times run-rate. The overlap is undisclosed and unbounded, and Traya's book cannot be read because no Q3 LK is archived.

The residual is labelled a book floor; for an estate carrying a FY2026E EBITDA loss of Rp4.3bn, book is an upper bound, not a floor. The report says the opposite in section 4 ("a loss-making estate does not obviously deserve one times revenue"), so the two statements pull against each other.

The VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT output contract asks for look-through earnings and leverage and a dividend-upstream coverage ratio. The report states that no dividend has ever been paid but does not compute the coverage (zero) or the look-through leverage of the operating base.
The gate lint returns 6,050 words against a 500-3,500 house range for an update, and only one valuation method is available (no cross-check survives negative earnings and the contaminated P/BV).
